fields.v: Evaluates; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — defines specification–oracle gaps (tests that depend on names, paths or literals the natural-language task specification does not state), builds a static audit for five languages, and evaluates SWE-Milestone v1.0.2 (98 graded milestones, 35 published agent runs) in depth plus four further benchmarks (SWE-EVO, SWE-Chain, SWE-bench Verified, DeepSWE) from public data; no agents run by the author

fields.v: 25 of 98 milestones have a hard hidden dependency (0.6% of required tests at risk; go-zero 15/23 milestones, 7.1% of tests). Blocked units fail in 80.6% of runs vs 48.4% for comparable units (lift 1.67, 95% CI 1.32-2.04; odds ratio 4.64, CI 2.92-7.37); stated names make no difference (1.08). Renaming one hidden name breaks the unit in 126 of 128 Go cases. Ranking robust (tau-b 0.984 score / 0.942 resolve for 28 runs), within random-removal variation; all 34 neighbouring run pairs have overlapping 95% rank intervals. Other benchmarks: a third or more of tasks affected where specifications are release notes or LLM summaries (SWE-EVO 17/48, SWE-Chain 64/155), almost none where screened or written for tests (Verified 3/500, DeepSWE 7/113 flagged, 1 confirmed); SWE-Chain lift only 1.12 because its harness isolates failed imports and reports them back. Runs reproduce 45% of hard and 79% of inferable hidden names

fields.v: Audit precision 58/65 (89.2%, Wilson 79.4-94.7%), recall 13/14 (92.9%); reproducible (identical results on repeated runs). Limitations stated: realisation is observational and groups may differ in difficulty; counterfactual covers Go only; some rules set on development data (DeepSWE not out-of-sample); lexical SRS matching; name-level extractors without type checking; behavioural gaps covered only by a heuristic, so counts are a lower bound; cross-benchmark comparison not controlled; addenda not yet tested with agent runs

fields.v: Limitations as stated in the Limitations section (observational realisation, Go-only counterfactual, rules tuned on development data, lexical matching, name-level extraction, behavioural gaps a lower bound, one benchmark in depth, correlational memorisation analysis, addenda effect not measured). Gaps/recommendations: run a dependency audit when generating specifications and state the names, paths and messages the tests need or exclude tests that reach into internals; replay references in several topological orders; isolate build units and report unresolved names to the agent; publish per-test results. Cause: generator prompts tell the LLM not to over-specify implementation details
